name: Program Name
description: Official consumer-facing name of the loyalty program.
benchmark_notes: Track renames (e.g., British Airways Executive Club → The British Airways Club, April 2025; Hilton HHonors → Hilton Honors, 2017; GrabRewards → GrabCoins).

name: Operator Company
description: Legal entity or brand operating the program day-to-day.
benchmark_notes: May differ from brand (e.g., PAYBACK GmbH operated under Loyalty Partner GmbH within American Express Group).

name: Parent Company
description: Ultimate parent/controlling company of the program operator.
benchmark_notes: Key for coalition and JV programs (e.g., Scene+ owned ~33.3% each by Scotiabank, Cineplex, Empire; flybuys 50/50 Coles–Wesfarmers).

name: Sector
description: Primary industry sector of the program.
benchmark_notes: Cross-sector programs (e.g., Amazon Prime, Walmart+) map to 'other' or their dominant monetization sector.

name: Primary Region
description: Geographic footprint of the program.
benchmark_notes: Use 'global' only for genuinely multi-continent programs; otherwise pick the dominant operating region.

name: Launch Year
description: Year the program launched (or year of current form after merger/rebrand).
benchmark_notes: Reference points: AAdvantage 1981, Star Alliance 1997, Hilton HHonors 1987, Marriott Bonvoy merger 2019, Skywards 2001.

name: Program Archetype
description: Structural type of the loyalty program.
benchmark_notes: Umbrex playbook archetypes: points, tiers, paid memberships, coalition, experiential; Open Loyalty adds account credits and gamification as primary frameworks.

name: Primary Objective
description: The single primary behavioral objective the program funds at launch.
benchmark_notes: Loyalty Juggernaut: one primary objective at launch, others sequenced behind it; four behavioral types — frequency, basket size, retention, data/identity.

name: Tier Count
description: Number of status tiers including entry level (excluding base non-status members if distinct).
benchmark_notes: Industry norm is 3–5 tiers (Talon.One); Marriott Bonvoy has 5 elite tiers above base; Hilton Honors has 4 status levels.

name: Tier Names
description: Ordered list of tier names from lowest to highest.
benchmark_notes: Examples: Hilton (Member/Silver/Gold/Diamond), Qantas (Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum/Platinum One), AMC Stubs (Insider/Premiere/Premiere Go/A-List).

name: Tier Structure Type
description: Shape of the recognition layer: flat, tiered, or hybrid.
benchmark_notes: Loyalty Juggernaut recognition layer has three broad shapes; hybrid combines tiers with transactional perks (e.g., AMC Stubs free tier + paid A-List subscription).

name: Qualification Metric
description: Primary metric used to qualify for status.
benchmark_notes: Shift to spend-based qualification is a notable trend (British Airways moved to spend-based tier points from April 2025: £7,500 Silver / £20,000 Gold annually).

name: Qualification Thresholds per Tier
description: Threshold value required for each tier in the qualification metric's unit.
benchmark_notes: Reference values: Marriott Silver 10 / Gold 25 / Platinum 50 / Titanium 75 / Ambassador 100 nights + $23,000 spend; Sephora VIB $350 / Rouge $1,000 annually; Qantas status credits 300/700/1400/3600.

name: Qualification Window
description: Period over which qualification metrics accumulate.
benchmark_notes: ALDO uses rolling 12-month ($150/$300); many airlines use qualification year + 12-month status period.

name: Status Period Length
description: How long earned status lasts once qualified.
benchmark_notes: Common norm: 12-month status periods; benchmark against qualification window alignment.

name: Downgrade Policy
description: Rule governing status loss when requalification fails.
benchmark_notes: Design norm: maximum one-level downgrade (soft landing); e.g., Marriott Titanium with zero qualifying nights drops only to Platinum, not to base.

name: Status Grace / Extension Period
description: Grace or extension mechanics offered on status (e.g., 90-day extensions, rollover nights).
benchmark_notes: Post-pandemic programs normalized status extensions and night rollovers; benchmark whether extensions are automatic or promotional.

name: Tier Membership Distribution
description: Share of active members in entry / mid / top tiers.
benchmark_notes: Design target: 60–70% entry, 20–30% mid, 5–10% top (Talon.One).

name: Top-Tier Exclusivity
description: Percentage of total members in upper and top tiers.
benchmark_notes: Norm: upper tiers (silver/gold/platinum) <10% of base; top tier ≈0.5% of members (Open Loyalty).

name: Status Match Availability
description: Whether the program offers status matches from competing programs, and under what terms.
benchmark_notes: Record match source list, documentation requirements, challenge vs instant match, and how long matched status lasts.

name: Base Earn Rate
description: Primary earn rate for the core qualifying action (points/miles per currency unit, per mile, or per night).
benchmark_notes: Normalize to points per 1 local currency unit or % of spend for cross-program comparison.

name: Earn Currency
description: Name and unit of the loyalty currency earned.
benchmark_notes: Miles (airlines), points (hotels/retail), coins (GrabCoins), status credits (Qantas, non-redeemable), ShowPoints (Audience Rewards).

name: Earn Metric Basis
description: Whether earning is based on distance flown, cabin, spend, nights, or transactions.
benchmark_notes: BA's 2025 move from distance/cabin tier points to spend-based tier points is an industry reference point.

name: Bonus Multiplier Structure
description: How elite, promo, or partner multipliers stack on base earn.
benchmark_notes: Record whether multipliers stack multiplicatively or additively, and caps.

name: Partner Earning Network
description: Size and type of partners that can earn the currency (transfer-in, direct earn, portals).
benchmark_notes: Examples: Chase Shop and Earn 1–15 pts/$ at 1,000+ stores; Nectar 14 member companies and 400+ online retailers (2010).

name: Promo Mechanics
description: Standard promotional levers used (double-point days, challenges, streaks, gamification).
benchmark_notes: T-Mobile Tuesdays is a partner-perks promo model; Starbucks Stars redesign (March 2026, Gold at 500 Stars) shows earn-threshold promos.

name: Welcome / Enrollment Bonus
description: Bonus given on enrollment or first qualifying action.
benchmark_notes: Card examples: Barclaycard Avios free card 5,000 Avios on £1,000 spend in 3 months; Avios Plus 25,000 on £3,000.

name: Earn Caps and Exclusions
description: Limits on earning (per transaction, per period, excluded categories).
benchmark_notes: Qantas charges a A$99.50 join fee — enrollment cost is itself an earn-side parameter.

name: Redemption Options
description: Catalog of redemption categories available.
benchmark_notes: Chase UR: travel, cash back, 200+ gift-card brands, transfers; Lidl Punkte redeems against streaming subscriptions (Disney+, BILD+).

name: Transfer Partners
description: External programs to which currency can be transferred, with ratios.
benchmark_notes: Amex MR transfers only to participating airline programs; Bilt transfers to ~19 airline programs and 7 hotel groups; record transfer ratio and transfer time.

name: Redemption Value per Point
description: Effective cents-per-unit value (CPP/CPM) for typical redemptions.
benchmark_notes: Anchor: flybuys 2,000 points = A$10; PC Optimum 1,000 points = CA$1; AMC Stubs 5,000 points = $5 off.

name: Minimum Redemption Threshold
description: Lowest balance required to redeem.
benchmark_notes: PAYBACK redeems from 200 points; GrabCoins offsets from 50 coins.

name: Award Pricing Model
description: How redemption prices are set.
benchmark_notes: Dynamic pricing drives devaluation risk: award prices across 39 major airline/hotel programs rose ~37% 2015–2026 (~3.2%/yr), led by Delta SkyMiles +60% and Hilton Honors +55%.

name: Blackout Dates and Award Availability
description: Restrictions on redemption availability.
benchmark_notes: Record blackout dates, capacity controls, and whether partner awards are exempt.

name: Redemption Channels
description: Channels where redemption can occur.
benchmark_notes: DBS points redeem via DBS PayLah! including NETS QR acceptance points — QR/offline redemption is a differentiator.

name: Expiration Policy
description: Rules for currency expiry.
benchmark_notes: Reference trajectory: AAdvantage no expiration → 3 years (1989) → 18 months (2012) → 24 months (March 2022); Delta removed expiration 2011; United 2019; Cathay Asia Miles expire after 18 months of inactivity.

name: Devaluation History
description: Record of earn-rate cuts, award-chart increases, or benefit reductions over time.
benchmark_notes: Track date, magnitude, and type; cross-check against benchmark index of ~3.2%/yr award inflation 2015–2026.

name: Earn-to-Burn Ratio
description: Points issued versus points redeemed over a period.
benchmark_notes: No widely published primary benchmark; proxy via issuer disclosures of deferral vs recognition (e.g., AAdvantage 2025: deferred $4.445B, recognized $3.935B).

name: Breakage Rate
description: Estimated percentage of issued currency that will never be redeemed.
benchmark_notes: Delta recognizes breakage proportionally as remaining miles are redeemed; Marriott discloses a 1pp lower breakage estimate raises loyalty liability ~$50M; KPMG calls breakage a critical deferred-liability input.

name: Breakage Recognition Method
description: Accounting method used to recognize breakage revenue.
benchmark_notes: Delta: proportional recognition with statistical models; Cathay actuary: Probability(Redemption) + Probability(Breakage) = 1 under IFRS 15.

name: Point Liability Balance
description: Carried loyalty program deferred revenue / liability.
benchmark_notes: Reference balances (FY2024/2025): Delta $8.8B; Marriott $7.519B; American Airlines $10.564B (YE2025).

name: Liability Sensitivity to Breakage
description: Disclosed sensitivity of liability to a 1pp change in breakage estimate.
benchmark_notes: Marriott: −1pp breakage ≈ +$50M liability; 2024 estimate revisions reduced revenue and raised liability ~$72M.

name: Points as Collateral / Financing
description: Whether the program's value has been pledged or securitized.
benchmark_notes: Delta SkyMiles valued at $6.5B and pledged as collateral in 2020 after a 78% decline in miles redeemed in H1 2020.

name: Enrolled Member Count
description: Total enrolled members.
benchmark_notes: Known figures: Hilton Honors 270M+ (official fact sheet, Oct 2026); Accor ALL 100M (2025); Qantas FF 18.9M (June 2026); AAdvantage 115M (April 2021); Amazon Prime ~220M (mid-2025).

name: Active Member Count
description: Members active within a defined period (12 months typical).
benchmark_notes: Active/engaged ratio is a core health metric; Air Miles Netherlands reports 3.8M active.

name: Partner Network Size
description: Count of earn/redemption partners (coalition members, transfer partners, co-brand merchants).
benchmark_notes: PAYBACK: 30+ in-store partners across 22,000+ German stores and ~700 online shops; Rakuten Rewards US: 3,500+ stores.

name: Geographic Coverage
description: Countries/markets where the program operates.
benchmark_notes: Examples: Amazon Prime 28 countries; Tesco Clubcard UK/IE/CZ/SK/HU; Hertz ~160 countries.

name: Member Share of Volume
description: Share of total business volume generated by members.
benchmark_notes: Marriott: loyalty members booked 72% of U.S. and 65% of global room nights in 2024.

name: Alliance / Network Scale
description: Scale of alliance or multi-brand network the program plugs into.
benchmark_notes: Star Alliance: 26 members, ~1,300 airports, 195 countries, two-tier alliance rewards (Silver/Gold).

name: Mobile App Availability
description: Whether a dedicated app exists and its core functions.
benchmark_notes: Record earn, redeem, card wallet, mobile order, push offers, digital membership card.

name: Website / Member Portal
description: Self-service web portal for balance, redemption, and profile.
benchmark_notes: Baseline requirement; benchmark depth (statement, partner marketplace, challenges hub).

name: API / Open Platform
description: Availability of public or partner APIs for earn/redemption integration.
benchmark_notes: Open Loyalty benchmark includes data/integration as a readiness dimension; 28.6% name integration as top challenge.

name: Digital Wallet Integration
description: Support for Apple/Google wallets, in-app barcode, QR redemption.
benchmark_notes: Table stakes in retail/dining; differentiator in emerging markets via QR (e.g., DBS/NETS QR).

name: Personalization and Data Capability
description: Ability to segment and personalize offers from first-party data.
benchmark_notes: Open Loyalty Benchmark 2027 scores AI readiness as one of seven dimensions; 53.6% define success via retention/CLV.

name: Co-branded Credit Cards
description: Co-branded card programs attached to the loyalty currency.
benchmark_notes: Record issuer, earn rate, annual fee, and elite-qualifying benefits; e.g., PC World Elite Mastercard earns 30 pts/$ at Loblaw affiliates.

name: Alliance / Coalition Membership
description: Airline alliance, hotel alliance, or coalition membership.
benchmark_notes: Alliances: Star Alliance, oneworld, SkyTeam; coalitions: PAYBACK, Air Miles, Scene+; hotel: GHA Discovery.

name: Cross-Industry Partnerships
description: Named partners outside the core sector (retail, fuel, streaming, dining).
benchmark_notes: Examples: Amazon Prime fuel discount at 7,500+ BP/Amoco/ampm; Walmart+ fuel at ExxonMobil/Murphy USA + Paramount+/Peacock + Burger King Royal Perks link.

name: Transfer-In Partners
description: Programs whose currency can be converted into this program's currency.
benchmark_notes: Distinct from transfer-out; e.g., Barclaycard Avios sweeps monthly into The British Airways Club.

name: Lounge Access Benefit
description: Lounge access by tier (own lounges, partner networks, guest allowances).
benchmark_notes: Core airline/hotel elite differentiator; record guest limits and third-party lounge programs (e.g., Priority Pass attach).

name: Upgrade Policy
description: Complimentary or prioritized upgrades (cabin/room) by tier.
benchmark_notes: Record eligibility, confirmation windows, complimentary vs miles-based, and clear vs waitlist.

name: Priority Boarding / Check-in / Security
description: Priority processing benefits by tier.
benchmark_notes: Star Alliance Silver/Gold include priority boarding and upgrades as alliance-level incentives.

name: Late Checkout / Guaranteed Availability
description: Late checkout, guaranteed room availability, and related hotel elite perks.
benchmark_notes: Record guaranteed 4pm checkout rights by tier and whether they are subject to availability.

name: Dedicated Support
description: Dedicated elite lines, ambassadors, or concierge.
benchmark_notes: Marriott Ambassador Elite: $23,000 + 100+ nights — top-tier service as a monetizable perk.

name: Experiential / Event Rewards
description: Access to events, concerts, previews, and unique experiences.
benchmark_notes: ALL Accor Live Limitless positions experiences centrally; F1 membership (Aston Martin I/AM) is an experiential archetype.

name: Fee Waivers and Service Perks
description: Baggage fee waivers, free award changes, breakfast, wifi, etc.
benchmark_notes: Bundle all cost-avoidance benefits; material to perceived value at mid tiers.

name: Revenue Model
description: How the program makes money.
benchmark_notes: Qantas Frequent Flyer reported A$625M underlying EBIT in FY2025–26 — loyalty as a standalone profit center.

name: Membership Fee Structure
description: Free vs paid tiers, join fees, and subscription pricing.
benchmark_notes: Reference: Qantas join fee A$99.50; Costco Executive $130/yr (Sept 2024); Walmart+ $98/yr; ALL Accor+ paid cards (Jan 2026); Barclaycard Avios Plus £20/month.

name: Profitability Disclosure
description: Whether program-level profit/EBIT is publicly disclosed.
benchmark_notes: Qantas discloses loyalty EBIT; airlines disclose loyalty revenue and liability in 10-Ks even without full P&L.

name: Deferred Revenue Flow
description: Annual deferral of revenue on points issued versus recognition on redemption/breakage.
benchmark_notes: AAdvantage 2025: deferred $4.445B, recognized $3.935B; Delta 2024: $7.1B loyalty revenue recognized ($3.8B travel awards + $3.3B other).

name: Audit Risk Profile
description: Whether breakage/fair-value estimates are flagged as significant audit risks.
benchmark_notes: EY used an actuarial specialist to assess Delta's mileage breakage estimate — a benchmark for estimate complexity.

name: Partner Revenue Sharing
description: How points economics are shared with coalition and transfer partners.
benchmark_notes: Record currency sale price to partners, breakage sharing, and redemption settlement terms.

name: KPI Measurement Set
description: Metrics used to judge program success.
benchmark_notes: Umbrex KPI set: enrollment, activation, repeat rate, frequency, AOV, CLV, redemption, retention; 53.6% of surveyed firms use retention/CLV as the success definition.

name: Program Maturity Level
description: Maturity stage of the program against an industry model.
benchmark_notes: Use a consistent maturity model (e.g., Umbrex 8-chapter playbook maturity model; Open Loyalty 7-dimension readiness score).

name: Regulatory Constraints
description: Legal/regulatory limits affecting program design.
benchmark_notes: Reference: Norway banned domestic airline loyalty programs in 2002 to promote competition and lifted the ban in 2013; accounting standards (IFRS 15/ASC 606) govern liability.

name: Gamification Elements
description: Games, streaks, badges, challenges, and non-transactional engagement mechanics.
benchmark_notes: Gamification is one of Open Loyalty's four primary frameworks; Club Canela awards 5 points per 5 minutes streamed (engagement earn).

name: Paid Membership Layer
description: Whether a paid membership/subscription layer sits on top of the free program.
benchmark_notes: Examples: Amazon Prime (~220M), Costco (81.4M paid memberships, Feb 2026), Walmart+, Disney+, Uber One, AMC A-List, ALL Accor+, Instacart+.

name: Breakage Reversal Risk
description: History of reversing previously recognized breakage when redemption expectations change.
benchmark_notes: Southwest reversed $116M of prior breakage revenue in Q4 2024 for pandemic-era flight credits expected to be redeemed.
